## Finding verdicts (re-verified at tip)

- **RH-27 (code half) — CONFIRMED.** `infra/pulumi/monitoring.ts` built exactly ONE
  `webhook_tokenauth` channel to the ops-alert sink, gated on `rhema:opsAlertWebhookUrl`
  (construction sites at the old lines 93–103; `notificationChannels: channels` on the two policy
  sites at 275/312), and the sink only writes an `ops_alert_received` log line — per
  `docs/ops/on-call.md`, receipt is not a page. No `email` channel, no mobile leg, zero
  `UptimeCheckConfig` in `infra/`, no test-page arm recorded.
- **RH-20 — CONFIRMED.** ADR-054 says the §13.5 error-budget burn alert ">2×" is "already
  implemented for the availability SLO" — the `gcp.monitoring.Slo` resource existed (old line
  341) but **no AlertPolicy consumed it**; exactly two `new gcp.monitoring.AlertPolicy`
  construction sites existed (route-5xx + the SLO-signal map), and the monitoring test pinned
  that count. The spec'd row is `API availability, monthly 99.9% | error-budget burn > 2×`
  (design-spec §13.5, `rhema-design-spec.md:2719`).
- **RH-21 residual — CONFIRMED.** `packages/contracts/src/observability.ts`
  `formatRouteErrorLine` emitted a fixed allowlist with **no `serviceContext`** — Error
  Reporting grouped the lines but could never attribute a release. The image-baked
  `RHEMA_BUILD_GIT_SHA` already rides both services' env (JOURNEY.1 `/healthz` provenance),
  so the version stamp had a source; it was never threaded into the error line.
- **RH-22 — CONFIRMED.** Zero `UptimeCheck` anywhere under `infra/` and no `conditionAbsent`
  policy: a dead edge (never emits a 5xx line) or a dead worker (the `slo.probe` breach lines
  only exist on breach) produced no signal at all.

## Changes

**`infra/pulumi/monitoring.ts`** — the four findings, in one file (the file header comment now
records the channel model honestly: a catcher log line is receipt, not a page).

- **Channels (RH-27).** `channels` is now a derived list of up to three legs:
  (a) the existing `webhook_tokenauth` channel (unchanged, `rhema:opsAlertWebhookUrl` secret);
  (b) NEW `email` NotificationChannel `rhema-${stack}-ops-email`, gated on secret config
  `rhema:opsAlertEmail` — the operator fills the key (`pulumi config set --secret`), no personal
  address is committed, and secret-config keeps the address encrypted in stack state;
  (c) NEW mobile leg bound by name: `rhema:opsMobileChannelName` carries the paired channel's
  `projects/<p>/notificationChannels/<id>` resource name into every policy. **Judgement call,
  verified:** GCP's Monitoring API refuses `mobile_app` channel create/get/update (404 —
  console pairing is the only mint path; the Terraform data-source gap is the same API
  limitation), so the program CANNOT build the channel — the scaffolding is the config-key
  binding + the recorded deferral, exactly "they only pair, don't build".
- **Burn-rate (RH-20).** `apiBurnRatePolicy` — `conditionThreshold` whose `filter` is the
  time-series selector `select_slo_burn_rate("projects/<p>/services/api-<stack>/
  serviceLevelObjectives/api-availability-<stack>", "3600s")`, `COMPARISON_GT` threshold `2`,
  duration `0s`, `dependsOn: [apiAvailabilitySlo]`. The 3600s lookback is the documented burn
  window for a monthly budget (the API doc's canonical example); the spec row records only
  ">2×" — the threshold is the spec's literal, the window is the documented default, recorded
  here as the judgement call.
- **Uptime (RH-22 + RH-27).** `UptimeCheckConfig` per public-domain host — `domains.app` +
  `domains.api`, `GET /healthz` over TLS every 60 s, content-matched on the healthz handler's
  literal `"ok":true` (a parked-host 200 still fails). Domain-less stages get none — a
  `*.run.app` origin would only prove the GFE answered (VERIF.2 / F-OPS.1-10), so `domains` is a
  new `MonitoringArgs` input wired from `cfg.domains` in index.ts. `uptimeFailPolicy` pages when
  ≥2 checker regions fail inside the 300 s window (`ALIGN_NEXT_OLDER` + `REDUCE_COUNT_FALSE`;
  one region's blip is a transient, not a page). Only built when checks exist — a zero-condition
  policy is invalid.
- **Absence (RH-22).** `uptimeAbsentPolicy` — `conditionAbsent` ×N: the `check_passed` metric
  silent for 900 s per check (the check pipeline itself dead — the failure alert cannot see
  that), plus `run.googleapis.com/container/billable_instance_time` silent for 900 s on the
  worker service — the worker is `minInstances: 1` `cpuBilling: "instance"` (always-on stage
  fact), so a live worker emits points continuously and 15 min of silence is the dead-worker
  class the finding names.
- Every policy site carries `notificationChannels: channels` — the construction-site count the
  old test pinned at 2 is honestly 5 now (route-5xx + the signal map + burn + uptime-fail +
  absent), and the test pins the new total.

**`infra/pulumi/index.ts`** — `rhema:opsAlertEmail` (`getSecret`), `rhema:opsMobileChannelName`
(plain `get` — a resource name, not a secret), and `cfg.domains` threaded into
`createMonitoring`.

**`packages/contracts/src/observability.ts`** — RH-21: `RouteErrorFields` and
`RequestLogContext` gain optional `serviceVersion`; `formatRouteErrorLine` always emits
`serviceContext.service` (the allowlisted service name) and `serviceContext.version` when a
sanitized stamp was provided (`sanitizeServiceVersion` — `[\w.:+\-/]{1,80}`, env-derived but
still validated at the emit seam, upholding the nothing-user-sourced contract). `routeErrorLine`
binds `serviceVersion` from the context like requestId/trace — Omit'd from the field override
so a call site cannot forge the release stamp; direct `formatRouteErrorLine` callers may set it.

**`apps/api/src/observability.ts` + `index.ts`**, **`apps/web/src/observability.ts` +
`server.ts`** — `requestContext(gcpProject, serviceVersion?)` (backward-compatible second arg);
both composition roots pass `deps?.buildGitSha ?? process.env.RHEMA_BUILD_GIT_SHA` — the same
image-baked value `/healthz` already surfaces, so the Error Reporting release matches the
deploy-provenance SHA.

## Judgement calls

1. **`mobile_app` cannot be provisioned.** Verified the API limitation before choosing the
   binding-by-name design — creating a resource would fail at `up`; the honest scaffolding is
   the config key + the deferral that names the operator's three remaining acts.
2. **Email via `getSecret`, mobile name via `get`.** The on-call address is personal data —
   secret-config keeps it encrypted in stack state and out of plaintext state exports; a
   notification-channel resource name is not a secret.
3. **Burn window = 3600s.** §13.5 records only "error-budget burn > 2×" on the monthly SLO; the
   1-hour lookback is the documented selector example for a monthly budget — recorded rather
   than invented.
4. **2+ failing regions on uptime.** A single-region checker failure is a GCP-side transient;
   `REDUCE_COUNT_FALSE > 1` pages on a real edge-down without paging on blips.
5. **Dead-worker detector = `billable_instance_time` absence**, not a log-line absence — the
   worker emits no periodic log when healthy (the `[slo]` lines exist only on breach), and the
   always-on posture makes the platform metric continuous.
6. **Absence alerts bind `channels` like the rest** — consistent; on a stack with no channels
   configured they still record incidents.
